All 8 boundary conditions have at least one owner module with handling path: BC-001→be-auth-service(FM-013,FM-014), BC-002→be-auth-service(FM-015,FM-016)+mp-api-client(FM-003), BC-003→mp-ws-client(FM-005,FM-007)+be-session-manager(FM-024), BC-004→be-post-service(atomic increments documented in topology notes)+PostgreSQL constraints, BC-005→be-message-service(FM-021)+be-ws-handler(FM-012), BC-006→be-post-service(FM-017), BC-007→mp-pages(subpackage architecture documented in topology notes), BC-008→be-core(FM-025). Add concurrency test contracts during implementation.

Layered architecture consistent throughout. Routes (orchestration) → Services (business logic) → Repositories (data access) → Models (entities). No gap >1 level. Frontend mirrors with Pages → Components + Client adapters.

One cycle found and annotated: mp-api-client ↔ mp-auth. This is a bootstrapping dependency — mp-auth calls the login endpoint via mp-api-client during authentication flow, and mp-api-client reads JWT from mp-auth for auth headers. This is an acknowledged intentional cycle (annotated in topology notes). Backend dependency graph has zero cycles. All services depend inward toward models with no back-references.
All 22 modules have explicit extension_points and sealed_points declarations in their Module Specs. No module is fully open or fully closed without documented reason.

All 28 failure modes have complete propagation paths from point of failure to point of handling. No failure terminates in undocumented 'log and swallow' or panic. Each FM specifies: trigger → behavior → propagation → handler. Frontend failures propagate via event system (auth-expired, ws-disconnected) to app-level handlers. Backend failures propagate via exception hierarchy → FastAPI exception handlers → structured JSON responses.

All mutable state has exactly one owner: JWT tokens → mp-auth, connection state → mp-ws-client, active WS connections → be-session-manager (with asyncio.Lock coordination documented), DB pool → be-core, database tables → be-models (coordination via PostgreSQL transactions). No state has multiple owners without explicit sharing declaration.

deferred.reason: Research references recommend Redis for caching and rate limiting. Design uses in-memory rate counters and DB-level caching for MVP. Conscious ponytail simplification — adding Redis for <10k users is speculative infrastructure. Rate limiting via in-memory counters is sufficient for MVP; migration path to Redis documented in research conclusion.
deferred.risk_accepted: Rate limit counters reset on server restart. Session-less JWT means no Redis for token blacklist — tokens are valid until expiry. Acceptable for MVP; add Redis if token revocation becomes a requirement or rate limiting needs persistence.

evidence.pass: All 28 failure modes have at least one test_contract defined (35 contracts total). Each contract specifies scenario, type (UNIT|INTEGRATION|PROPERTY), and verifies field. All contracts use valid type enum values.
